note: Franky's notebook. Written by the duck itself (the model's weights never change). tries = attempts the note was shown in, wins = how many of those succeeded.

knowledge.text: Walking forward (e.g., attempts 21, 24) can stop early if the target is right at the feet.
Closing the beak does not guarantee picking up the banana even when the beak sense indicates very close proximity (e.g., 0.06 m, 0.04 m).
Combined search find(what='yellow banana and green box') successfully located both objects (e.g., attempt 17).
Pickup fails if the banana is behind the beak tip (e.g., 0.02m behind in attempt 28).
The banana's long side orientation is consistently angled away from the direction faced (e.g., -16 degrees in attempt 38).
System issues a warning if the last 5 tool calls resulted in no movement or successful pickup.
Beak closure fails if the sensor reports the banana is more than 0.10 m from the beak tip, even when visually close (e.g., 0.19 m).
Movement commands are not perfectly precise; requesting 0.10 m forward sometimes results in slightly less distance (e.g., attempt 29: 0.09 m).

skills.text: When positioning for pickup, use small, incremental walks (e.g., 0.05 m) to ensure the target is within striking distance.
Before closing beak, ensure the banana is slightly ahead of the beak tip and centered relative to the duck's axis.
Use small incremental walks to achieve precise alignment before attempting pickup.
Use turns of 30 degrees or more when attempting alignment on the spot, as small turns are imprecise.
After moving, always re-run find(what='yellow banana and green box') to confirm the objects' current relative positions.
